industry: Off-highway wheels, tires, and undercarriage (Tier-1 OEM supplier to Deere, AGCO, CNH, CAT, Kubota); Carlstar (consumer/powersports/trailer) integration in progress since 2/29/2024 acquisition

drawdown_context.filing_date_close_context: Aggregate market value of non-affiliate float was ~$360M at 6/30/2024 on 63.2M shares out (i.e., ~$5.70 prior implied); MHR Repurchase executed 10/18/2024 at $7.20/sh, a depressed-but-not-distressed level. The 5-year performance graph in the 10-K shows TWI at $189.42 vs $100 invested on 12/31/2019 (down from a 2022 peak of $427.37 = -55.7% drawdown from peak), badly trailing the S&P 600 Ag & Farm Machinery index ($156.00) and the S&P 500 ($182.05). The drawdown into the 5/15/2025 cutoff reflects: (a) collapse of FY24 operating income from $148.7M to $33.2M (-77.7%); (b) FY24 net loss of $3.6M; (c) negative organic demand in ag and EMC segments masked only by the Carlstar revenue addition; (d) overhang from AIP S-3 shelf (declared effective Dec 2024) plus standstill termination after the 2025 annual meeting; (e) 7.00% senior secured notes due 2028 trading discount given EBITDA compression; (f) tariff/cycle uncertainty layered on top.
drawdown_context.control_note: delisted_or_distressed group. Forensic framework should produce a meaningfully ELEVATED composite — multiple Mode B tells (auditor change after Carlstar close, related-party MHR buyout funded with new debt at the trough, AIP S-3 dilution overhang, ag/EMC operating income collapse, revolver utilization rising into the print, no dividend, deferred tax realizability CAM) cluster in a single 12-month window. This is the bear pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm:] 'We have served as the Company's auditor since 2024. /s/ BDO USA, P.C. Chicago, Illinois February 26, 2025.' [Second opinion:] '/s/ GRANT THORNTON LLP We served as the Company's auditor from 2012 to 2023. Southfield, Michigan February 29, 2024.' [Exhibit Index Item 16(r):] 'Letter dated March 19, 2024 from Grant Thornton LLP.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: auditor_change_tracker. (A) Does the registry confirm the transition (8-K Item 4.01 + Exhibit 16 letter)? (B) The timing tell — auditor was replaced AFTER 11 years of Grant Thornton tenure within ~3 weeks of the Carlstar acquisition closing (2/29/2024) and Carlstar's audit/PCAOB-history footprint moved with the deal. Auditor changes are most-discriminating when they cluster with material transactions; this one clusters with a $312M acquisition AND a related-party share buyout in the same calendar year.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9/Exhibit 16 + Grant Thornton letter dated 3/19/2024 + BDO opinion dated 2/26/2025 (cik 0000899751 EDGAR; pre-cutoff Form 8-K 0000899751-24-000036 filed 3/19/2024)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Auditor changed: Grant Thornton (2012-2023, 11-year tenure) -> BDO USA, P.C. (since 2024). The transition occurred immediately after Carlstar acquisition close (2/29/2024) and was formalized via 8-K Item 4.01 dated 3/19/2024 with Grant Thornton's required Item 304(a)(3) letter as Exhibit 16. BDO's FY24 audit identified its only Critical Audit Matter as 'Realization of Certain Deferred Tax Assets' — i.e., the new auditor IMMEDIATELY surfaced a judgment area on the very first audit. Grant Thornton (in its retrospective opinion on 2022/2023, dated 2/29/2024) explicitly disclaimed any opinion on the adjustments BDO made to apply the segment recast and revised accounting policies retrospectively ('We were not engaged to audit, review, or apply any procedures to the adjustments to retrospectively apply the change in accounting described in Note 1').
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: tier-2 auditor replacing tier-2 auditor (Grant Thornton -> BDO; not Big 4 to Big 4) on the same day as a $312M leveraged acquisition is a yellow-to-orange tell. The fact that BDO immediately raised a deferred-tax-realizability CAM AND that Grant Thornton's retrospective opinion explicitly disclaims responsibility for the segment/policy recast adjustments creates an attestation gap exactly at the transition seam. Combined with C3 (related-party buyout) and C8 (segment results collapse), this pattern fits the Signal OS auditor-change-near-capital-event red zone.

rfm_tuples.R: [BDO Critical Audit Matter:] 'Realization of Certain Deferred Tax Assets... the Company has gross deferred tax assets of $174.3 million as of December 31, 2024, reduced by [valuation allowance]... We identified the Company's evaluation of the realizability of certain deferred tax assets as a critical audit matter as significant management judgment is required in evaluating and weighing the collective positive and negative evidence... included the Company's assessment over the ability to generate sufficient future taxable income.' [Note 19:] 'The Company continues to record a valuation allowance in several major jurisdictions, including various U.S. states, Italy, and Luxembourg as these amounts remain more likely than not that the deferred tax assets would not be utilized... The Company did not release a valuation allowance in 2024 and released a valuation allowance of $0.6 million on the net deferred tax asset in 2023... The Company has $65.6 million of gross federal net operating loss carryforward... $324.9 million of gross [foreign NOLs].'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: existence check on the CAM language and DTA balances. MODE B: implied-verification — a DTA realizability CAM is the GAAP-permitted way for an auditor to flag durable doubt about generating taxable income. Combined with the FY24 net loss ($3.6M) and 143.4% effective tax rate (i.e., tax expense > pre-tax income), the math says the parent's U.S. entity is generating losses while paying taxes on foreign earnings.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 19 Income Taxes + BDO CAM + FY24 P&L (effective tax rate 143.4%)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Gross DTAs $174.3M; ongoing valuation allowances in the U.S. (states), Italy, and Luxembourg (the major operating jurisdictions). ZERO valuation allowance release in 2024 vs $0.6M release in 2023 — the trajectory is the wrong way. U.S. federal NOL carryforward $65.6M; foreign NOLs $324.9M. Effective tax rate 143.4% in FY24 vs 23.7% in FY23. Open tax years U.S. 2021-2024, Brazil 2018-2024, Italy 2018-2024 — long audit exposure tails in the U.S., Brazil, and Italy match exactly the jurisdictions where the FX/operating drag is worst.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A + B: the auditor's CAM is functionally a soft going-concern signal at the segment level — the U.S. and European entities cannot credibly demonstrate future taxable income to support full DTA realization. While no Substantial-Doubt / Going-Concern language appears (and would not be expected given $174.4M consolidated cash at 3/31/2025), the CAM combined with rising valuation allowance posture is the strongest forensic tell within a tax footnote and ties directly to the operating income collapse in C8.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Item 5 + Note 15 Stockholders' Equity:] 'On October 18, 2024, the Company entered into a Stock Repurchase Agreement (the "Stock Repurchase Agreement") with MHR Capital Partners Master Account LP... MHR Capital Partners (100) LP... and MHR Institutional Partners III L.P. (together, the "MHR Funds", a related party). Pursuant to the Stock Repurchase Agreement, the Company purchased in a privately negotiated transaction from the MHR Funds, and the MHR Funds sold to the Company, an aggregate of 8,005,000 shares (the "MHR Shares") of the Company's Common Stock, at a per share price of $7.20 per share, for aggregate cash consideration equal to $57.6 million (the "MHR Repurchase").' [Financing cash flows section:] '...$45.0 million borrowed to fund the $57.6 million repurchase of the Company's common stock from the MHR Funds, a related party, in October 2024.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: capital_allocation_tell — the textbook negative pattern is a related-party / activist insider exit at a depressed price, financed by NEW REVOLVER DEBT (not cash from operations) at the bottom of the operating cycle. Compare to the open-market authorization ($50M Dec-2022 program), which had only $1.0M left as of 12/31/2024 — the company effectively replaced an undirected program with a directed insider liquidity event.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 5 Issuer Purchases table + Note 15 + Note 4 (revolver draw) + Form 4 cluster 10/21/2024 + SC 13D/A 10/21/2024 (accession 0001193125-24-240513)
rfm_tuples.M_value: MHR Funds (Mark Rachesky / 13D filer dating back years) exited 8.005M shares (~12.7% of pre-deal share count) for $57.6M at $7.20/sh in a privately negotiated transaction, $45M of which was funded by NEW REVOLVING CREDIT DRAWS. The $50M open-market repurchase program (Dec 2022) had been used down to $1.0M of remaining capacity — so 'optionality' was already exhausted before the directed buyout. The MHR price ($7.20) was BELOW the price at which the open-market authorization had bought stock earlier in 2024 (open-market WAVG $7.42), demonstrating MHR's willingness to exit at any liquidity-providing bid. SC 13D/A filed same day 10/21/2024 confirms MHR's ownership reduction.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: this is the canonical 'company defends the price by absorbing a related-party insider exit with newly borrowed money' pattern. Three confirming Mode B layers: (1) financed with new debt at a moment when ag/EMC operating income was already in free fall; (2) MHR is an explicit related party (board-affiliated; SC 13D filer); (3) executed before the FY24 print revealed the $115.5M YoY collapse in income from operations. The forensic interpretation: insiders had information about operating trajectory and chose to monetize while the company simultaneously diluted equity for AIP (Carlstar consideration) and added leverage.

rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: confirm S-3 was filed and made effective. MODE B: derive the dilution math the filing doesn't explicitly highlight — Carlstar consideration included 11,921,766 shares of newly issued common stock at $168.7M implied value (Note 15 equity rollforward, 2024), which became registered-for-resale on AIP's S-3. Combined with standstill expiry at the 2025 annual meeting, the overhang structurally floors the share price.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K + Q1 2025 10-Q forward-looking-statements section + S-3 accession 0001193125-24-249938 filed 11/1/2024 (effective Dec 2024)
rfm_tuples.M_value: AIP (American Industrial Partners) received 11,921,766 shares of TWI common stock as part of the Carlstar consideration (per Note 15 equity rollforward 2024). S-3 filed 11/1/2024 and declared effective in Dec 2024 — i.e., AIP CAN sell into the open market without further registration friction. Standstill TERMINATES after the 2025 annual meeting (June 2025 window, just AFTER the 5/15/2025 cutoff). rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A confirms the structural setup; Mode B is the asymmetry: AIP holds ~18.9% of basic shares (11.92M / ~63.2M outstanding as of 2/18/2025) with a clear, declared exit pathway scheduled within ~5 weeks of the cutoff. Inserting MHR's exit (C3, 12.7%) on the buy side AT THE SAME TIME the company is contractually preparing for AIP's exit on the sell side is the textbook 'inside the trade' pattern — management knew which counterparties were on which sides of the float.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Note 4 Debt + Item 7 Debt Restrictions:] 'With outstanding letters of credit totaling $9.9 million and $146.0 million in borrowings under the revolving credit facility, the net amount available for borrowing under the credit facility at December 31, 2024 totaled $21.2 million.' [Q1 2025 10-Q:] 'With outstanding letters of credit totaling $5.4 million and $163.0 million in outstanding borrowings under the revolving credit facility, the net amount available for borrowing under the new credit facility totaled $56.6 million at March 31, 2025.' [10-K:] 'The Company was in compliance with these debt covenants at December 31, 2024.' [Q1 2025 10-Q:] 'The Company was in compliance with these debt covenants at March 31, 2025.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: existence check on covenant compliance assertion. MODE B: derive the trajectory the filing doesn't headline — revolver BORROWINGS rose from $146.0M (12/31/2024) to $163.0M (3/31/2025), +$17M in 90 days, into a SEASONALLY STRONG quarter (sales rose $107M vs Q4 2024). The borrowing-base 'available for borrowing' jumped from $21.2M to $56.6M only because AR/inventory expanded seasonally, NOT because the company paid down debt.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 4 + Q1 2025 10-Q Note + Item 7 Liquidity (cik 0000899751 EDGAR)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Revolver balance: $146.0M (12/31/2024) -> $163.0M (3/31/2025), +11.6% QoQ in a typically working-capital-INTENSIVE-not-paying-down quarter. Borrowing base at 12/31/2024 = $177.1M (i.e., revolver was already 82% utilized of available base at year-end). $400M of 7.00% senior secured notes due 2028 are FULLY DRAWN by definition. Covenant restrictions include a fixed-charge coverage ratio test of 'not less than 1.0 to 1.0 (calculated quarterly on a trailing four quarter basis)' that activates when availability falls below $17M or 10% of credit-facility limits — i.e., the covenant trigger sits ~$4M away from the 12/31/2024 cushion ($21.2M - $17M = $4.2M). The Q1 2025 'in compliance' assertion is technically true but the spring trade-cycle working capital was the only thing keeping the covenant springing trigger inactive at year-end.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the springing fixed-charge covenant is one bad quarter (or one inventory writedown) away from activation. Headline language 'in compliance with all covenants' is true but reads very differently with $4M of cushion to the springing trigger. Total debt $585M against TTM EBITDA of arguably $130-140M (op income $33M + D&A) = ~4.3x leverage at year-end, climbing with each quarter of ag/EMC underperformance. This is the financial fragility signal that a delisted/distressed group member should display.

No other customer accounted for 10% or more of Titan's net sales in 2024, 2023, or 2022.' [Exhibit Index 10.10:] 'Global Long-Term Agreement dated November 1, 2024 between Titan International, Inc. and Deere & Company.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: Deere share trend confirmation. MODE B: the framework's 'concentration is a tell when share is shrinking' filter — Deere's share went 15% -> 13% -> 11% (-400bp over 24 months) while total revenue was flat (Carlstar masking). Deere's absolute purchases imply ~$203M (2024) vs ~$237M (2023) vs ~$326M (2022), a 38% decline in Titan's largest customer over two years. The Nov 1, 2024 Global Long-Term Agreement renewal is a Mode A positive but the share erosion is the more important Mode B signal.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Deere & Company share: 11% FY24 / 13% FY23 / 15% FY22 (-400bp over 24 months). Implied absolute Deere revenue: ~$203M / ~$237M / ~$326M -- a -37.7% drop from FY22. Top-10 OEM share: 35% / 40% / 43% (-800bp over 24 months) -- diversification trend, but in the WRONG direction (declining share to ALL major OEMs, not just rebalancing). Deere LTA was renewed 11/1/2024 (Exhibit 10.10) but no economic terms are public; the share trajectory suggests volume commitments, not pricing, were the negotiation lever.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the customer concentration disclosure is technically diversifying ON A PERCENTAGE basis, but the underlying absolute Deere dollars dropped 38% in 24 months. This is concentration risk EXPRESSING ITSELF in real time. A new long-term agreement signed at the trough of Deere's destock cycle is the friend-of-the-house signal; whether it floors volumes will be visible in Q2 2025. The base-rate concern: when Deere/AGCO/CNH cyclical demand returns, Titan's market share of that recovery is questionable given the Carlstar pivot has redirected management attention to consumer/powersports/trailer (a structurally different category).

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Item 1A:] 'The Company currently owns 64.3% of Voltyre-Prom, a leading producer of agricultural and industrial tires in Volgograd, Russia, which represents approximately 5% and 7% of consolidated assets of Titan as of December 31, 2024, and 2023, respectively. The Russian operations represent approximately 5%, 6%, and 6% of consolidated global sales for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022, respectively.' [Note 15:] 'The Company and the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF) own all of the equity interests in Voltyre-Prom... Following the [Feb 1, 2022] transaction, the Company and RDIF's ownership remained at 64.3% and 35.7%, respectively, of Voltyre-Prom.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: existence check on Voltyre-Prom ownership / RDIF status. MODE B: derive the unspoken — RDIF (Russian Direct Investment Fund) is an OFAC-SDN-listed entity (sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury since Feb 28, 2022 under E.O. 14024). Titan's 35.7% partner in a sanctioned country IS a sanctioned counterparty. The filing acknowledges this exists but does not size the unwind cost or describe whether dividends/cash from Voltyre-Prom can legally be repatriated. Consolidated assets reduction from 7% to 5% YoY is consistent with the Russian operating environment but the de-consolidation pathway is not laid out.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1A + Note 15 + Note 16 VIEs (10-K) + OFAC SDN list (Mode B implied)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Voltyre-Prom: 64.3% Titan / 35.7% RDIF (OFAC-SDN since 2/28/2022). Russian assets declined from 7% to 5% of consolidated (year-over-year shrinkage, partly from ruble translation in OCI: $285.9M accumulated OCI LOSS at 12/31/2024 vs $219.0M loss at 12/31/2023, +$66.8M FX loss to equity). RDIF was issued 4,032,259 restricted Titan shares in Dec 2021 as put-option settlement; Titan repurchased those for $25.0M on 2/1/2022 — i.e., the entire RDIF equity arrangement is post-2014 sanctions exposure that the company has tried to ring-fence. The 10-K acknowledges 'restrictions on the ability of the Company to repatriate earnings and investments from international operations' but does not say which dollar value of Voltyre-Prom cash is currently stranded.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: ownership of a Russian subsidiary with a sanctioned RDIF partner is a tail risk that the framework should weight even though it is not the proximate cause of the drawdown. The fact that OCI losses on translation reached -$286M demonstrates the cumulative cost of holding the Russian asset; absent a disposal pathway (which the filing does not describe), this is a permanent equity drag. The Mode B 'where is the body buried' check is partially satisfied (Voltyre-Prom is disclosed, sized, and ring-fenced) but the disposal pathway question remains open into 2025.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K MD&A:] 'Income from operations for the year ended December 31, 2024 was $33.2 million, or 1.8% of net sales, compared to income of $148.7 million, or 8.2% of net sales, for 2023. The change in income was primarily due to lower net sales and the cumulative impact of the previously discussed items.' [Segment table 2024 vs 2023:] Agricultural income from ops $39.8M vs $100.6M (-60.5%); Earthmoving/Construction $7.0M vs $55.1M (-87.3%); Consumer $20.5M vs $22.4M (-8.5% despite +208.8% revenue from Carlstar). [Q1 2025 10-Q:] 'Net loss (7,861)' for Q1 2025.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: existence check on segment results. MODE B: the headline revenue number (+1.3% YoY to $1.85B) is essentially flat ONLY because Carlstar contributed $418.9M of revenue from 11 months. Removing Carlstar, organic revenue was approximately $1,427M (vs $1,821.8M in 2023) = -21.7% organic decline. Operating income organic decline is even worse — substantially all of FY24 op income came from segments that DECLINED.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Organic revenue decline: ~-21.7% (excluding Carlstar contribution). Agricultural segment income from ops -60.5% YoY ($39.8M vs $100.6M). EMC -87.3% ($7.0M vs $55.1M). Consumer +Carlstar but income still down -8.5% YoY ($20.5M vs $22.4M) on $320M of revenue gain — i.e., Carlstar added MORE revenue than COMPETITIVE consumer business contracted, but it added ZERO incremental operating income. The Q1 2025 10-Q shows the trajectory continues into 2025: agricultural segment income $9.4M vs $24.0M prior year quarter (-60.8% YoY for the SECOND consecutive year-over-year period at that magnitude). Q1 2025 consolidated net loss $7.86M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the Carlstar acquisition was timed at the top of the off-highway cycle (closed 2/29/2024) and immediately diluted operating margins (Consumer segment $90.99M gross profit / $20.5M op income = 19.2% gross margin but only 4.3% op margin — Carlstar SG&A loaded the segment). FY24 organic operating income excluding Carlstar contribution is approximately $12.7M (= $33.2M total - $20.5M consumer), down 91.4% from FY23. The collapse is the trigger for everything else: the deferred-tax CAM (C2), the MHR buyout funded with new debt (C3), the revolver utilization climb (C5), and the customer share erosion (C6) all read coherently as symptoms of a cycle-trough year that the company's M&A timing made worse.

rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Item 5:] 'We have not paid dividends on our Common Stock in recent years. The declaration and payment of future dividends is at the discretion of our Board of Directors, subject to any covenants contained in agreements to which we are a party. Refer to "Item 7 - Management's Discussion and Analysis of Liquidity and Capital Resources - Liquidity and Capital Resources" for further discussion on debt restrictions associated with payment of dividends.' [Debt covenants:] '...Limits on dividends and repurchases of the Company's stock...'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: dividend trajectory confirmation. MODE B: contrast with control-group survivors who RAISE dividends into drawdowns (e.g., ANDE raised div twice during the 2-year window) — TWI has no dividend to defend or to signal stability with. The capital allocation choice was entirely directed at insider-related buyouts (MHR $57.6M) at a moment when revolver headroom was thin.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Dividend: NONE (cut years ago, not resumed even during 2022/2023 peak earnings of $148.7M op income). Capital return mechanism is exclusively share repurchase ($50M Dec-2022 plan, used to $1.0M remaining; MHR $57.6M directed buyback). The Q1 2025 10-Q lists 'Limits on dividends and repurchases of the Company's stock' as an active covenant restriction under the revolver — i.e., even if the Board wanted to initiate a dividend, the springing covenant economics would govern.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: absence of a dividend trajectory removes the single strongest 'we are not in distress' signal that a Board can send. Capital return was concentrated 78% in a single directed related-party buyout (MHR) at the lowest moment of the cycle — the OPPOSITE of the diversified-ratable-buyback pattern seen at honest disclosers. Combined with the covenant restriction on future dividends and the fact that $1.0M of authorization remains (effectively spent), there is no Board-level signaling instrument left available to defend the equity story between 5/15/2025 and the next 10-K.
